title: Streaming SDK patterns and tool adaptor PRD
content:
Purpose:
This doc is an engineering-focused PRD sketch for a set of SDK patterns and lightweight runtime adaptors to make streaming responses, tool calling, and structured/typed output ergonomic for application developers using the Hosted API. Intention: pragmatic, implementable proposals that minimize breaking changes to current SDKs while enabling safer tool integrations and repeatable parsing for downstream pipelines.

Why this now:
- Customers adopting streaming for latency-sensitive apps report duplicated effort to implement robust incremental parsing + tool handoffs.
- We need a standard handshake pattern for tool calls so SDKs can automatically manage model->tool lifecycle (invoke, surface errors, retry).
- Structured output (JSON, typed records) is increasingly required by platform teams; ad-hoc prompt parsing leads to fragile pipelines.
- Current hosted-sdk prototypes show divergent patterns across languages; unify core primitives.

Primary goals:
- Provide a minimal streaming primitive across SDKs that supports: chunked tokens, interim deltas, and message-level boundaries for tool events.
- Define a tool-calling protocol (lightweight) that supports: manifest/descriptor for callable tools, safe input marshaling, explicit accept/decline flow from model to SDK, and fallback to text responses.
- Introduce a structured-output spec (typed schema hints + deterministic parsing rules) and SDK helpers to validate/repair output.
- Prioritize developer ergonomics: concise APIs, clear error semantics, and zero-config sensible defaults.

Non-goals:
- Not a full GHAS-level secure execution framework. Tool gating and permissions are out-of-scope for this iteration (we will coordinate with security/compliance).
- Not a complete rework of existing SDKs; aim for small surface additions and opt-in flags.

User personas & use cases:
- Product engineer building chat-based assistant that must call internal calendar and code-exec tools. Needs reliable, resumable tool handoffs and stable parseable outputs for downstream rules.
- Platform/integration engineer needing typed embeddings and JSON records emitted by models for analytics ingestion. Wants automatic validation and repair suggestions.
- Mobile engineer implementing token-by-token streaming to render UI progressively with low overhead.

Core design proposals (high-level):
1) Streaming primitives (SDK-level):
   - Primitive: StreamEvent (enum) delivered on a stream callback: {token, delta, chunk, boundary, tool_event, structured_fragment}.
   - SDKs should expose two main stream handlers: on_token(token_str), on_event(StreamEvent). on_event surfaces higher-level events (tool call start, tool call end, structured output start/end, parsing error).
   - Backpressure: provide a flow-control hint mechanism. For UI clients, a simple token buffer limit (default 1024 tokens) is fine; server will continue to stream but SDK exposes paused state for consumer to request resume.
   - Interim answers: support a partial_text() that concatenates safe deltas; SDKs should provide a sequence_number so UI can dedupe.

2) Tool-calling handshake (protocol sketch):
   - Tool descriptor: small JSON manifest (name, version, input_schema, auth_hint). Model emits a tool_call event with descriptor reference and serialized args.
   - SDK flow: when tool_call event received, SDK invokes registered local adaptor matching descriptor.name. Adaptor receives args + context, returns ToolResponse (status, output, error_code).
   - Model acceptance: After tool returns, SDK sends a ToolResult event back to the model via the same streaming channel; model may continue generation or emit an explicit "final".
   - Failure modes: adaptor can return "decline" (not permitted or missing auth) -> SDK sends ToolDecline event and model fallback path should be followed. Retries: SDK provides configurable retry policy for transient adaptor errors with jitter/backoff.
   - Security: adaptor invocation runs in the calling app's process — SDKs should surface hooks for platform teams to implement permission checks. (See security notes below.)

3) Structured output spec (typed fragments):
   - Hints vs hard contracts: model can emit a structured_output_start event with an optional JSON Schema/avro/schema-ref. This is a hint; SDK should attempt to parse streamed fragments into that schema incrementally.
   - Deterministic parse: SDK will collect tokens until chunk boundary or schema-validated fragment complete. If validation fails, SDK will attempt simple repairs (fill missing fields with nulls, coerce numeric strings). Repairs are surfaced via on_event(parse_repair, details).
   - Partial emission: SDK exposes on_structured_fragment(fragment_json, sequence_id, is_final) so downstream can begin processing before full object completion.
   - Canonical serialization: SDK provides a to_canonical_json() helper to produce newline-delimited JSONL for downstream ingestion.

4) SDK ergonomics and API examples (JS + Python sketches):
   - High-level goal: 1–2 function calls to opt-in to advanced behaviors. Keep default behavior backward compatible.

   Example (JS, pseudocode):
     const stream = client.responses.stream({model: 'r1', prompt});
     stream.on('token', (t) => renderToken(t));
     stream.on('tool_call', async (call) => {
       const res = await toolRegistry.invoke(call.name, call.args);
       if (res.status === 'ok') stream.sendToolResult(call.id, res.payload);
       else stream.sendToolDecline(call.id, res.error_code);
     });
     stream.on('structured_fragment', (frag) => ingestRow(frag.json));

   Example (Python, pseudocode):
     with client.stream_responses(model='r1', prompt) as s:
         for ev in s:
             if ev.type == 'token': print(ev.token, end='')
             elif ev.type == 'tool_call':
                 res = tool_registry.invoke(ev.name, ev.args)
                 s.send_tool_result(ev.id, res)

   - Defaults: SDK will convert model-emitted tool descriptors into a simple local adaptor registration pattern: register_tool(name, fn).

5) Compatibility & rollout strategy:
   - Phase 0 (opt-in): introduce experimental flags in SDKs: enable_tool_handshake, enable_structured_streaming. No default change to existing streaming endpoints.
   - Phase 1 (beta): surface helpers in official SDKs (JS/Python/Go). Provide migration docs and sample apps. Start collecting telemetry on common tool patterns and schema types.
   - Phase 2 (GA): enable structured hints by default for specific routes (e.g., /responses with schema param) and recommend manifest versioning for tools.

6) Observability & debugging:
   - SDKs should log canonical events: tool_call.received, tool_invoke.success/fail, parse.validate.fail, parse.repair.applied. Keep logs structured and include correlation ids.
   - Console: product will add a per-request timeline view showing token streams and tool events (future work).

Success metrics (initial):
- Developer time to integrate streaming+tool calls reduced by 50% (measured via internal sample apps & partner onboarding).
- Reduction in parsing-related production incidents (missing/invalid JSON ingestion) by 70% for customers opting into structured_streaming.
- 90th percentile tool-call latency (sdk adaptor execution) < 200ms for local adaptors in common runtimes.

Risks & open questions:
- Model behavior: how reliably will LLMs emit a clean tool_call event vs freeform text? We will iterate with curated prompt templates and eval sets. (See eval ticket API-512).
- Security: automatic invocation of local adaptors presents a risk surface. Need a gating policy and auth hints in descriptor. Security team must sign-off before Beta.
- SDK surface proliferation: keep minimal helpers to avoid fragmentation across languages.
- Backwards compatibility for existing streaming apps — ensure opt-in model until GA.

Implementation notes & TODOs (engineering):
- Build wire-format proposal for StreamEvent (compact enum over websocket + JSON payload for structured events). (OWNER: Jian)
- Prototype JS stream helper and tool registry. (OWNER: Priya)
- Add incremental JSON schema validator in Python SDK (OWNER: Liam)
- Create evaluation harness with 20 prompts that exercise tool-call fallbacks and structured repairs. (OWNER: Maya)
- Security review checkpoint and threat modeling. (OWNER: Elena)

Open questions to resolve in next sync:
- Should tool descriptors be signed/verified? If so, where is key management hosted?
- What default retry policy should SDKs expose for adaptor invocation?
- How should billing/metrics attribute tool execution time (model vs adaptor)?

Appendix: example event sequence (simple):
1) Client starts stream.
2) Model emits tokens, then emits tool_call event: {id: t1, name: 'calendar:create', args: {...}}
3) SDK receives tool_call, invokes local adaptor calendar.create(args) -> returns success + url. SDK sends ToolResult(t1, payload) to model.
4) Model resumes generation, emits structured_output fragment with partial JSON. SDK validates fragment; emits parse_repair if necessary.
5) Stream finalizes; SDK exposes final structured object and canonical JSON.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic; focus comments on SDK surface area and safety controls.
- Please add concrete examples of common tool manifests you expect to support in the linked Confluence page.
